notes.title: New look!
notes.notes: [p]Game development is rarely linear. [/p][p]You chip away at a big block of marble and you're sure there's a statue somewhere in there. Sometimes a big chunk of marble falls off and all of a sudden everything looks different.[/p][p]Out of the convoluted metaphor - I swear it made more sense in my head - we started looking at improving the visuals of TNU and we ended up drastically changing the look of the game. To give you an example of the scope of the change... this is the same level:[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45443809/c9035c6e8058016682c426e2399f7a43d43a7657.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45443809/0592c3d9a6582dc20d28e30c9e482bfee678dd8b.png"][/img][/p][p]Our team expanded with an additional artist - hi Adam - and a level designer - hi Ed - and their works has been invaluable in making this improvement happen.[/p][p]You can also find a new version of our trailer in the store page. Give it a look, and stay for the post credit scene.[/p][p]Aside from that, development on everything else has not slowed down. So we now have more levels, more obstacles, more gadgets, better controls and much more. But there will be time to talk about that.[/p][p]The road ahead is still long (ish?) but the statue starts to take shape.[/p][p]Yes, I am mixing metaphors.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45443809/b0cd85675e750da7b2e57788c237e3db8ecedb36.gif"][/img][/p]

notes.title: One good news, one bad news
notes.notes:
Hello! We have been deep at work to improve TNU. So much so that we have something pretty big cooking. We are working on expanding and improving pretty much every part of the game.

Because of this, we feel the demo is not representing the quality of the project any more (neither the screenshots and trailer, but that's a problem for another day). For this reason, we decided to delist the demo. A new demo will come (soon?) and more news even sooner.

Till the next time!

notes.title: Bubbles and milestones
notes.notes:
Steam Fest is over, the demo is published and it was time for us to get into what’s next.

Every time there is a delivery coming, it’s common to sort of stop working on anything new and focus on improving what’s in the game, and this time was no exception.

Now that demo and Next Fest are done, we are hard at work making some changes and adding new stuff. We are also taking the feedback we got from people who played the game and see how to integrate that into the game.

But mostly, we are focusing on making new gadgets, obstacles and levels: we are aiming at a release before the end of 2025, so the time to add new things is now.

As a designer, this is usually one of the most fun parts of development: you get to finally try all the ideas that accumulated in the past few weeks and months. And today I can show a sneak peek at one of these ideas.

I have always loved the bubbles of Bubble Bobble, so a gadget that lets the player shoot big bubbles seemed like a good idea. In particular, I loved the idea that you can both get objects sucked into the bubble but also use it to jump on it. So I tried to implement this in our game.

As it often happens, the difference between a quick prototype and something that can be put in the final game is dozens of bugs, edge cases and weird behaviors and many, many hours of work.

But in the end, I think it turned out pretty nice, so here’s a new gadget: you can shoot bubbles and they capture movable objects into them until you pop them.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45443809/f1229c0e58a33e482201157a22fcb0f01e275221.gif[/img]

You can even use them as temporary platforms, if you don’t hit them too hard.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45443809/1434d119b84e7cb763854606beca7366b625c6bb.gif[/img]

We also found so many other special uses - how about this one: you can put a bomb inside a bubble and it doesn’t trigger, so you can use bubbles to safely transport bombs where you want them to be. 
I hope players will find more.

Till the next time!

notes.title: Demo available now!
notes.notes:
[b]It's out! [/b]The demo, it is. This is still a relatively early build of the game, but we believe it shows some of the things that make it special.

There are some things that are different from what the final game will be: there are fewer levels, fewer gadgets and the runs are short - also, needless to say, there might be bugs. But the core experience is pretty much there.

So, please play it and let us know what you think! We would love to hear what you liked and did not like about There's Nothing Underground!

(Bonus picture featuring art made by our awesome artist Zixuan He)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45443809/c375ca1eefa5f4ede31bbc6e7eab76c20ef01a02.png[/img]

notes.title: One problem, many (many) solutions
notes.notes:
If you saw our trailer, you know we say [b]"one problem, many (many) solutions"[/b]. One of the core ideas of There's Nothing Underground is that there can be puzzles and obstacles that have many possible solutions, possibly one we didn't even think about. The key to that concept is gadgets.

Gadgets are the tools that the player has to interact with the world of TNU. When we design a gadget we try to think of how clearly it presents itself (as we don't want tutorials or text descriptions), how fun it is to use and how it will interact with everything else. And when we mean everything, we mean everything.

Let's take our trusty hookshot. It's a staple of videogames: always fun, always useful. But so, how would a hookshot work in our game? When we design a gadget we try to give it as many uses as possible. So, in this case, we want the hookshot to be useful both to pull the player to something [b]and[/b] to pull something to the player.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45443809/b60a8b0a7bc80720ee2952e0752055c964f123d5.gif[/img]

If you shoot the hookshot to something unmovable, the hookshot will pull our Gustav to it. This is useful to bridge gaps, gain elevation and so on. But if you shoot this gadget onto something movable, then that thing will be pulled towards you. This means anything movable, including platforms without gravity and such.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45443809/83d3acd70050500c86b740e28ae40c03d9418826.gif[/img]

But there's more: the hookshot will leave its arrow planted into its target. So we made it so the player can use it as a platform to stand on.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45443809/894ee302312c1a7c95d14a3e26a6402a5d2ffe12.gif[/img]

Finally, the hookshot looks like it should damage what it hits. And so it can also be used as a projectile, to damage plants, barrels or vines. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45443809/3964b54feef5a310a7502d1ad939db29e47d1107.gif[/img]

And of course, our promise is that everything works with everything, which means that if you shoot a hookshot through an antigravity field you will see it twist its trajectory. Even when the effect is subtle like in this case, we believe putting effort into this details pays off.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45443809/13db5bf847bc412c6a68e63048f7aefe46e04b6a.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45443809/917e9f617b0828f7a631a9ac96358cfb12e01c70.png[/img]

As a designer, making sure that every tool the player can use has as many uses as possible is very, very hard. But it also, in our opinion, makes the game so much more creative and interesting.

So, as usual, keep following us for more news, announcements and info and don't forget to wishlist etc. etc.

Till the next time!

notes.title: The game has been announced, but what is it?
notes.notes:
Hello. I'm Ferruccio Cinquemani, game designer on There's Nothing Underground

We have been working on this game for a while so I thought it could be interesting to write a bit how we got to what you see in the trailer

The initial concept came from an amalgamation of many different ideas and many different games, including some that I personally worked on. Most of all, I became very fascinated by the idea of having [b]puzzles without a set solution[/b]. Games like The Legend of Zelda Tears of the Kingdom managed to create a beautiful balance between clever puzzles and players freedom and I wanted to explore that concept even more. I love the freedom typical of sandbox games but I love it even more when that freedom is mixed with the parts I like the most in linear games - some narrative, clear objectives etc. With time, I even started to think about how the roguelike structure of many games I like currently could be applied to such a concept. But that came a bit later.

The general concept, though, has been there from the very beginning, with a little character navigating 2D levels and using random gadgets to reach some idols to pick up, destroy, or move to another part of the level, in the most dynamic way possible. Even visually, the very first sketch I drew about the main character already shows pretty much the same vibe as the final one

The paper origin...

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45443809/aae53d07034179bb6ff3ba22b2d9d861f8b0e289.png[/img]

And the final(?) form:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45443809/63e0e6ce7b716419ed98f41386bf85f07b6fe559.png[/img]

While working on the prototype, I started to wonder who this character is and what's his objective. Slowly, and quite organically, the general setting emerged. I won't get too much into spoilers, but I was fascinated by the idea of an underground that is down and up at the same time; almost in space but not quite - hence the hovering asteroid. But there will be time to get more into it.

The gameplay took shape quite quickly. Even in this screenshot from the prototype, it's easy to see the general structure of the game as quite similar to what it is today

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45443809/00c6af614af5e64e840d9149c8a50546235ef418.png[/img]

For comparison, this is the same level as it looks today - all thanks to our wonderful artist Zixuan.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45443809/392c204e0cad4012caa346b182de37fad197ab84.png[/img]

My hope is to write regularly about more infos about the game, so if that sounds interesting please follow, wishlist etc. etc.

Till the next time!
